topic: Humans Are Closer to T-Rex Than T-Rex Was to Stegosaurus

claims.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex lived from about 69 to 66 million years ago, at the very end of the Cretaceous period.
claims.evidence: Tyrannosaurus rex lived from about 69 to 66 million years ago, at the very end of the Cretaceous period.

claims.claim: Stegosaurus lived from about 155 to 145 million years ago, in the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages of the Jurassic.
claims.evidence: Stegosaurus lived from about 155 to 145 million years ago, in the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages of the Jurassic.

claims.claim: The gap in time between the last Stegosaurus and the first Tyrannosaurus rex is roughly 76 to 89 million years.
claims.evidence: The gap in time between the last Stegosaurus and the first Tyrannosaurus rex is roughly 76 to 89 million years.

claims.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex went extinct about 66 million years ago, and modern humans are a recent species on that timescale — so T. rex is separated from modern humans by less time than it is separated from Stegosaurus. Do not state a precise 'modern humans appeared X years ago' figure; the claim only needs the human lineage to be far closer to the present than 66 million years, not an exact date.
